commands.name: startup-hook-skill
commands.description: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions. (user)

commands.name: seam
commands.description:
Decompose a change or a codebase into review SEAMS (core / link / environment / test) with Seam, serving Seam's LLM passes from THIS Claude session via spawned subagents instead of a `claude -p` subprocess — no `claude` binary, no PATH, no API key needed. Two modes: DIFF review (group a git diff's hunks into seams) and CODEBASE intent discovery (trace where a symbol/intent lives — a static footprint, or a DETERMINISTICALLY-grown one). Use when asked to "review by seam", "decompose this diff", "run Seam", "where does X live", "map the footprint of X", or to grow an intent across a codebase. ROUTING — reach for Seam when the answer is a PATH/FLOW/STRUCTURE across multiple files (how a feature works, where a flow ends, what's the blast radius, mapping a flow before editing it): prefer ONE Seam run over 4+ iterative greps to stitch a flow by hand.
FIRST DECIDE WHICH KIND OF QUESTION IT IS — this choice, not which shape, is what costs calls:
  • A PATH ACROSS SYMBOLS — "how does X work end to end", "trace X", "which modules participate",
    "where does the flow culminate", "where does it hit the database" → ONE FLOW GROW (§C):
    `--scan --auto --center <f>#<s> --intent "<question>" --skeleton --format agent`. It walks the
    whole path in a SINGLE call and opens with `## Persists / reads` — the anchor's own DB/route/event
    access lines with their source text.
  • ONE SYMBOL — "who calls X", "what breaks if I change X", "what does this module expose" → a SHAPE
    (§D, list below).
DO NOT answer a path question with per-symbol shapes. Every shape below is scoped to ONE symbol, so tracing an N-hop flow with them costs N calls — a grep loop with `--query consumers` as the verb. Measured (bench/grep-vs-seam, 2026-08-01): 11 of 23 shape calls across six runs were `--query consumers` re-anchored one hop at a time, for a question one grow call answers.
Seam ALSO answers non-flow STRUCTURAL questions as deterministic SHAPES (§D): who calls X — RESOLVED, no grep false-positives — (`--query consumers`), what X depends on (`--query dependencies`), the transitive blast radius / what breaks if you change X (`--query impact`), the FACTS to refactor X (`--query refactor` = impact+dependencies+contract; the PLAN stays yours), can A reach B + a witness path (`--query reaches`), a module's boundary (`--query contract`), the cohesive subsystem around X (`--query neighborhood`), how A and B differ (`--query compare`), **which HTTP ENDPOINTS a class serves — every `@GET`/`@POST`/`@Path` with its handler method, line and code — or where X touches the DATABASE or any cross-stack shared key** (`--query coupling`; ask it of the CLASS, it widens to the file when the routes are declared at class level), **who WRITES the state X reads** (`--query writers`), or EVERYTHING structural about ONE SYMBOL in one call (`--query brief` — start here when the question is about one symbol; for a PATH question use the flow grow above, not this); or `--ask "<question>"` (§E) ROUTES a plain question to the right shape. The discriminator: use Seam when the answer's correctness needs RESOLVED EDGES. For a quick one-fact lookup grep is still instant (Seam to MAP/VERIFY, grep to DRILL); for "what code is ABOUT X" (meaning, not edges) use embeddings/RAG — Seam routes those away honestly rather than faking them. FIRST CALL on an unfamiliar codebase is `--locate <name>` (symbol, file OR directory name -> every definition, one call, no opinion) — NOT find/ls/grep, which measurably burns 10+ calls hunting. Then give the pick as `--center file#symbol` (or several, comma-separated, for a multi-mechanism concern) — Seam skips center detection and traces+decomposes from it (~11s). `--center` is MANDATORY with `--intent`: the intent SHAPES the answer, it does not choose where to look. Don't know the symbol? `--locate <name>` prints every definition of a name and picks none. `--locate` to ORIENT, Seam to TRACE — grep only when `--locate` comes back empty. ALSO for INTERNAL PLANNING before implementing: if a change touches a LOGIC/DATA flow (a spine) you haven't mapped and understanding it would take 2+ symbol-discovery greps across files, run Seam FIRST (orient grep → named-center grow) to plan against a verified spine, not a guess — not just for "how does X work". NOT for presentation/display-only changes (layout/styling/visuals): no spine → noFlow, just grep/read. File-count alone doesn't trigger Seam — a flow to trace does. (project)

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: design
commands.description: Make a new Design artifact from a brief

commands.name: slides
commands.description: Make a new Slides deck artifact from a brief

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: artifact-diagramming
commands.description: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.

commands.name: artifact-capabilities
commands.description: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator
commands.description: Author or improve the run-<unit> skill - a per-project skill that tells agents how to build, launch, and drive this project's app. Use when the user asks to set up the project, get it running, write run instructions, or verify build/run steps work from a clean environment.

commands.name: docs
commands.description: docs (living docs people share, comment on and edit; use only when the user asks for one: names a doc, document, page, memo, spec, PRD, runbook or write-up, asks for somewhere to share or keep editing something, or says yes to your doc offer; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat (at most a one-line doc offer); a report, status update, recap or "something I can send them" with no form named → ask first: reply, doc or file?; tabs hold tables and live charts too; a pasted claude.ai/code/artifact/… link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; not HTML pages, apps or plain chat answers; a .docx/.pptx/.xlsx/PDF asked for by name → that format's skill): asked for one → no docs-connector instructions in context? call the docs connector's `guide` with topic.instructions first, then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached. Documenting code means docstrings or repo docs, not a doc. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: import-memory
commands.description: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: morning
commands.description: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pdf
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pptx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: skill-creator
commands.description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved. (claude.ai sync)

content.text:
I traced the full spine, from the React admin console through the TypeScript admin client transport, across HTTP, into JAX-RS and down to the model layer.

## Read path

1. **Client construction** — `js/apps/admin-ui/src/admin-client.tsx#initAdminClient` builds a `KeycloakAdminClient` pointed at `environment.adminBaseUrl` and registers a token provider backed by keycloak-js; `useAdminClient` exposes it. `js/libs/keycloak-admin-client/src/client.ts#KeycloakAdminClient` instantiates `this.realms = new Realms(this)`.

2. **Call site** — `js/apps/admin-ui/src/context/realm-context/RealmContext.tsx#RealmContextProvider` does `useFetch(() => adminClient.realms.findOne({ realm }), setRealmRepresentation, [realm, key])`, and publishes the result as `realmRepresentation` through `useRealm()`. That is the single realm read every settings tab consumes.

3. **Admin client** — `resources/realms.ts#findOne` is declared as `makeRequest({ method: "GET", path: "/{realm}", urlParamKeys: ["realm"], catchNotFound: true })`. `resources/resource.ts#makeRequest` delegates to `resources/agent.ts#request`, which splits payload into URL params / query params and calls the private `#requestWithParams`. That expands the URI template against `basePath` (`/admin/realms`), attaches `authorization: Bearer …`, and issues the call through `utils/fetchWithError.ts#fetchWithError`, decoding the body with `parseResponse`.

4. **Server** — `GET /admin/realms/{realm}` lands via `AdminRoot#getRealmsAdmin` (`@Path("realms")`) → `RealmsAdminResource#getRealmAdmin` (`@Path("{realm}")`, which resolves the `RealmModel`, sets it on the session context and builds the `AdminPermissionEvaluator` + `AdminEventBuilder`) → `RealmAdminResource#getRealm`. That method checks `auth.realm().canViewRealm()` and converts the model with `ModelToRepresentation#toRepresentation(session, realm, false)`, or falls back to a stripped-down representation for admins who may only list realm names.

## Update path

There are **two** write paths, and the realm-settings page uses the second one.

**(a) Generic** — `resources/realms.ts#update` is a `makeUpdateRequest({ method: "PUT", path: "/{realm}" })` → `resource.ts#makeUpdateRequest` → `agent.ts#updateRequest` → `#requestWithParams` (JSON-stringified body) → `PUT /admin/realms/{realm}` → `RealmAdminResource#updateRealm`. This is what OTP/WebAuthn/CIBA/password-policy tabs, `BindFlowDialog`, `RevocationModal`, `LoginTab` and `EventsTab` use.

**(b) The Realm Settings form** — `js/apps/admin-ui/src/realm-settings/RealmSettingsTabs.tsx#save` (reached from `RealmSettingsSection`) deliberately bypasses `adminClient.realms.update`: it merges the form values over the cached realm, serialises `acr.loa.map` / `acr.uri.map` attributes, and `fetchWithError`s a raw `PUT {adminBaseUrl}/admin/realms/{realm}/ui-ext` carrying a `UIRealmRepresentation` (realm + `upConfig`). That extra field is why it can't use the plain endpoint.

**Server dispatch for ui-ext** — `RealmAdminResource#extension` (`@Path("{extension}")`) looks up an `AdminRealmResourceProvider` by name; `AdminExtProvider#getId` returns `"ui-ext"` and `AdminExtProvider#getResource` returns `AdminExtResource`, whose `@Path("/")` sub-resource locator `AdminExtResource#realm` returns `UIRealmResource`. `UIRealmResource#updateRealm` delegates straight to `RealmAdminResource#updateRealm` and, only on a 2xx, additionally applies the user-profile config via `UserProfileResource#setAndGetConfiguration`.

**Core update** — `RealmAdminResource#updateRealm` requires `manage-realm`, blocks renaming `master`, runs `ReservedCharValidator` / SMTP / key-pair validation, then calls `RepresentationToModel#updateRealm`, which forwards to the datastore's `ExportImportManager#updateRealm` — implemented by `DefaultExportImportManager#updateRealm`, the method that actually renames the realm, reconciles attributes and writes every field onto the `RealmModel`. Afterwards it fires `StoreSyncEvent` and records an `OperationType.UPDATE` admin event, returning `204 No Content`.

Two notes on confidence: `agent.ts#requestWithParams` is a private field (`#requestWithParams`) — I list it under its bare name. `AdminExtProvider` is gated on `Profile.Feature.ADMIN_V2`, so path (b) exists only when the v2 console is enabled; path (a) is always present.

## ANSWER
